- Overweight recent sentiment spikes in forecast calibration; if sentiment rises sharply, reduce forecast overshoot.
- When sentiment turns negative (e.g., < 0.0), suppress upward momentum in forecast; avoid peak extrapolation.
- Model tends to overestimate early in 30-day horizon; apply downward bias to first 5–7 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct — adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14 day average if sentiment is fading.
- Forecasting spikes (e.g., >80) should be capped at +5–10% above prior peak unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative values (e.g., -0.21, -0.30), reduce forecast volatility and shift toward mid-range historical mean.
- Avoid forecasting “trend continuation” when sentiment is inconsistent or oscillating — favor short-term mean reversion over long-term trend.
